newsitem.title: PERU: Lima shares end narrowly mixed in low volume.
newsitem.headline: Lima shares end narrowly mixed in low volume.

text.p: Shares on the Lima stock exchange closed narrowly mixed Friday on meager volume as foreigners, concerned about the economy's growth prospects, sold blue-chips, while local players bought second-tier bargains.
Expecting no market-moving news, they added the exchange would be depressed next week because foreign investors would remain sidelined.
Friday, the General Index .IGRA rose 0.22 percent to 1,481.6 points and the blue-chip Selective Index .ISEL fell 0.96 percent to 2,063.8 points, according to preliminary stock figures.
"Trade on the exchange remained apathetic with foreigners selling because of the low expectations for economic growth towards the end of the year," said Cesar Germanda of local brokerage Peruval.
The government announced earlier this month that the economy grew 1.9 percent in the first nine months of the year, compared with 8.9 percent in the same period of 1995.
Thursday, benchmark Telefonica del Peru accounted for more than half of the day's volume and closed down 1.3 percent at 5.30 soles, on a preliminary count of 3.23 million shares.

In the electricity sector, after Merrill Lynch started coverage of Moyopampa -- formerly known as Edegel -- as near- and long-term accumulate, the distributor rose 2.19 percent to 1.40 soles, on a preliminary count of 479,000 shares.
Luz del Sur, which will see the sale of the state's 30 percent stake in the company start on Monday, also rose 0.86 percent to 3.53 soles on volume of 386,000 shares.
In a total of 1,303 trades, volume was estimated at 30.0 million soles ($11.7 million), including a 12 million sol cross-trade in Telefonica, brokers said.
